tweets.text:
The AI-native application market seems to be converging into 5 different structural archetypes:

Bucket 1: Headless primitives (Exa, Tinyfish); You basically choose to learn into the world where UIs are disposable

Bucket 2: Governed harnesses / Liability shields (@harvey , @FulcrumAI , @RogoAI , @OpenEvidence)

- Wrapping frontier models in workflow structure, permissions, citations, and output fidelity for high-stakes domains like legal and insurance 
-Some industries scared of using Claude / Codex too

Bucket 3: Context, Memory & Trigger Harness (@playerzero_ai , Hone, @useactively )
- they treat organizational reality, relationships, memory, and state changes as a first-class engineering layer rather than treating the prompt or the single app UI as the center of gravity

Bucket 4: Services as Software! @DecagonAI 
- self explanatory

Bucket 5: Personal Persistent Runtimes (@bot, Muse)
- Own the individual user’s persistent cloud computer, browser, and daily routines

Wow....  @kozyraki and Mendel Rosenblum know someone doing exactly this with a fully built out product  :) 

Leave it the Stanford PHDs to be ahead of the curve https://t.co/DKOfClwgku
AI's comparative advantage over people will end up being persistence not intelligence

Outcome per dollar is the frontier. We’re advancing it at every layer: FLOPs-efficient pretraining (MAI Base 2), long RL climbs (Rocket), and token-efficient models (seven new MAI models announced last week). All driving better economics for our customers.

By building models and products together, we can keep hill-climbing and building models that deliver real-world tasks and passing the gains directly to customers, while staying open to every frontier model.
